title.zh: BIS · Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors
title.en: BIS · Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors

sum.zh: In this interim final rule (IFR), the Department of Commerce is establishing new rules to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on U.S. technology to threaten U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. First, this rule establishes new restrictions which will apply for exports, reexports, or transfers (in-country) to overseas data centers that remotely supply significant volumes of compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau. These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models. Data centers, foreign foundries, and chip exporters are required to perform robust due diligence on their customers, including any direct or indirect ownership or control by persons in Country Group D:5 or Macau, as part of complying with this new control. The license requirement will not apply to commercial recommender systems, such as those used by online retailers or social media companies, as these functions do not pose the same national security threat. Second, in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil (and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State or the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs)--countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion. The license requirement for these five countries will not apply to semiconductors destined to companies headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent company is headquartered in, the United States, provided certain reporting requirements are met. Commerce will be actively monitoring for countries that tolerate evasion of this IFR and will consider a range of consequences for such countries, such as import restrictions, new license requirements on advanced semiconductor exports, downgrading the country's status in the U.S. export control regime, and Entity List designations and temporary export prohibitions for foreign persons involved in such activities. Third, this IFR amends the presumptions which front-end chips fabricators and chip packagers face when exporting advanced-node logic chips. These amendments reduce the number of pathways to overcome the presumptions for chip designers located in destinations which face a license requirement for SI chips. This change gives the U.S. government critical oversight over companies headquartered in certain countries that seek to leverage advanced semiconductor production capabilities in third countries. Finally, the IFR formally rescinds the regulations implementing the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule. The AI Diffusion Rule has never been enforced. The regulatory changes in this rule formalize the rescission of the AI Diffusion Rule, which the Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced in May 2025.

title.zh: Federal Register · Executive Compensation Disclosure Reform
title.en: Federal Register · Executive Compensation Disclosure Reform

sum.zh: The Securities and Exchange Commission ("Commission") is proposing amendments to its executive and director compensation disclosure rules to make the requirements more principles-based and to reduce compliance burdens for registrants, while maintaining the disclosure of material information to investors. The proposed amendments would focus the disclosures on the principal executive officer ("PEO") and principal financial officer ("PFO"), streamline the tabular disclosure requirements, and simplify and rationalize various other aspects of the compensation disclosure rules, including the Compensation Discussion and Analysis ("CD&A"), pay ratio, pay- versus-performance, and perquisites disclosure requirements.

title.zh: Federal Register · HIPAA Privacy Rule: Changes To Support Coordinated Care and Individual Engagement and Reduce Regulatory Burdens

sum.zh: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS or "Department") is issuing this final rule to modify the Standards for Privacy of Individually Identifiable Health Information ("Privacy Rule") under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) and the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health (HITECH) Act. title.zh: DHS · Notice of Revised National Environmental Policy Act Implementing Procedures
title.en: DHS · Notice of Revised National Environmental Policy Act Implementing Procedures

sum.zh: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS or Department) is updating DHS Directive 023, Implementation of the National Environmental Policy Act, which establishes procedures for complying with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA). This update is necessary in light of the recent rescission of the Council on Environmental Quality's NEPA implementing regulations, which DHS's procedures were designed to supplement. In addition, the update incorporates provisions from the Fixing America's Surface Transportation Act, the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act; and the Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 related to the environmental review process. The updated Directive promotes collaboration and efficiencies in the implementation of NEPA and modernizes the processes and procedures for environmental review. This update enables DHS to conduct coordinated, consistent, predictable, and timely environmental reviews, thus reducing unnecessary burdens and delays. The draft Directive is being made available for public review and comment. These comments will inform development of the final Directive. Upon finalization, the Directive will rescind DHS Directive 023-01, Rev 01 and DHS Instruction 023-01-001-01, Rev 01 which were issued in 2014.

title.zh: FCC · National Television Multiple Ownership Rule
title.en: FCC · National Television Multiple Ownership Rule

sum.zh: In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) repeals the national television multiple ownership rule (national cap), which prohibits a commercial television licensee from having a cognizable interest in television stations that have an aggregate national audience reach above 39%. The Commission finds, given seismic changes in the modern media marketplace, that the rule's repeal will help empower local broadcast television stations to operate in the public interest and to better serve the needs and interests of their local communities. The Commission will review on a case-by-case basis proposed transactions that would have been prohibited under the national cap to determine whether a proposed transaction would serve the Commission's media ownership goals of localism, competition, and viewpoint diversity.

title.en: BIS · Guidance and Procedures for Implementing Tariff Adjustments for Specialty Pharmaceuticals and Associated Pharmaceutical Ingredients and Technical Corrections to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States for Duties Imposed Under Proclamation 11020

sum.zh: This notice defines the pharmaceutical products and lists the jurisdictions that are eligible to receive an ad valorem tariff rate of zero pursuant to Presidential Proclamation 11020 of April 2, 2026, "Adjusting Imports of Pharmaceuticals and Pharmaceutical Ingredients Into the United States," (Proclamation 11020). These pharmaceutical products include drugs and associated ingredients where all approved indications are designated as orphan; nuclear medicines; plasma derived therapies; fertility drugs; cell therapy product; gene therapy product; antibody drug conjugates; medical countermeasures related to chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats; and animal health. Proclamation 11020 states that such products and associated ingredients receive the Section 232 zero tariff rate if they are products of a jurisdiction that has a current or forthcoming trade and security framework agreement or if they meet an urgent U.S. health need. This notice also includes procedures for the public to submit information for the Department of Commerce's (Commerce) approval to determine if imports of the pharmaceutical products and associated ingredients meet an urgent U.S. health need. This notice also issues five technical corrections to Annex I and one technical correction to Annex IV of the Proclamation.
